title: Nieuwe Republiek
capsule: The Nieuwe Republiek (New Republic) was a small Boer state established in 1884 in northern Natal, present-day South Africa, by volunteers under Lucas Johannes Meyer who had aided Zulu king Dinuzulu in the Zulu succession war and claimed roughly 13,600 km² of territory as payment. Its capital was Vryheid; Germany and the South African Republic (Transvaal) recognised it, while Britain recognised it in 1886 but severed it from the sea by annexing its coastal strip. Diplomatically untenable and economically weak, the republic voted to incorporate itself into the Transvaal on 20 July 1888. After the Second Anglo-Boer War the Vryheid district passed to the British Colony of Natal in 1903.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The republic's borders derive from a formal Boer-Zulu land grant and British colonial surveys; territorial extent is reasonably well attested, though some edges were contested.
